lore_summary.en: Esfandiyar's son rules with grief and ambition. The Kayanian house turns on itself.
lore_summary.fa: بهمن پسرِ اسفندیار بود و می‌دانست پدرش به خاطرِ ترسِ گشتاسپ مُرد. وقتی تخت را گرفت به زابلستان لشکر کشید. فرامرز مقاومت کرد و شکست خورد. خانه‌ی زال شکسته شد. بهمن صد سال درست حکم کرد.

scenes.body_en: Bahman was Esfandiyar's son, and he came of age knowing exactly what had been done to his father and why. Goshtasp had sent Esfandiyar to chain Rostam not because Rostam had rebelled — he had not — but because Goshtasp feared his own son's popularity and needed Esfandiyar to fail or die at a safe distance from the throne. Esfandiyar walked into the mission with his eyes open, fulfilling the king's command because he had given his word and his word was the thing he would not break even in a trap. He died for his father's fear. Bahman inherited that knowledge the way a child inherits a wound that never fully heals.
scenes.body_fa: بهمن پسر اسفندیار بود، و بزرگ شد در حالی که دقیقاً می‌دانست با پدرش چه شده و چرا. گشتاسب اسفندیار را نفرستاده بود که رستم را در بند کند چون رستم سرکشی کرده بود — نکرده بود — بلکه چون گشتاسب از محبوبیت پسرش می‌ترسید و به اسفندیار نیاز داشت که در فاصله‌ای امن از تخت شکست بخورد یا بمیرد. اسفندیار با چشمان باز به درون ماموریت رفت، فرمان شاه را انجام داد چون سخنش را داده بود و سخنش چیزی بود که حتی در تله نمی‌شکست. برای ترس پدرش مُرد. بهمن آن آگاهی را به ارث برد، آنطور که کودکی زخمی را به ارث می‌برد که هرگز کاملاً التیام نمی‌یابد.

scenes.body_en: When Bahman came to the throne — after Goshtasp's long dim years — he proved himself a more capable ruler than his dynasty had produced in a generation. He administered the kingdom with precision. He kept the borders. He held court without the tantrums that had characterized his grandfather's reign. But he also marched on Zabulestan.
scenes.body_fa: وقتی بهمن به تخت رسید — پس از سال‌های تاریک و طولانی گشتاسب — خود را فرمانروایی کارآمدتر از آنچه سلسله‌اش در یک نسل به دست آورده بود نشان داد. پادشاهی را با دقت اداره کرد. مرزها را نگاه داشت. بدون طغیان‌هایی که نیاکانش را مشخص می‌ساخت دربار کرد. اما به زابلستان هم لشکر کشید.

scenes.body_en:
He marched not because Zal had done anything wrong — Zal, now ancient, had been the most faithful servant of the Kayanian house across five generations. He marched because Faramarz, Rostam's son, stood between the house of Bahman and the completion of a debt. Faramarz made the stand that his father never had to make, and lost. The house of Zal, which had held Iran's border through war after war that its kings started and its warriors finished, was broken at last.

Bahman ruled for a long time after. The chronicle gives him over a hundred years in its mythological reckoning, and those years were not hollow. Justice was administered. The kingdom was orderly. The borders held without the constant crises that had required a Rostam to solve them. In a narrower sense, Bahman succeeded at everything he attempted. But the Shahnameh treats his rule with a complexity it reserves for figures who are simultaneously right and wrong — men who achieve what they set out to achieve without that achievement being clean. He destroyed the line that had been more faithful to Iran than any king Iran had ever produced. He did it correctly. He did it completely. The victory and the loss were the same act.

Near the end of his reign, Bahman made a decision that shaped the next generation's story more than any battle he had fought. He named his daughter Homay as his heir.
scenes.body_fa:
لشکر نه کشید چون زال کار اشتباهی کرده بود — زال، حالا پیر، وفادارترین خادم خانه کیانی در پنج نسل بوده بود. لشکر کشید چون فرامرز، پسر رستم، بین خانه بهمن و تکمیل یک بدهی ایستاده بود. فرامرز آن مقاومتی را کرد که پدرش هرگز مجبور به کردنش نشده بود، و شکست خورد. خانه زال که مرز ایران را در جنگ بر جنگی که شاهانش آغاز کرده و جنگجویانش به پایان رسانده بودند نگاه داشته بود، سرانجام درهم شکست.

بهمن پس از آن مدت مدیدی حکومت کرد. روایت در حساب اساطیری خود بیش از صد سال به او می‌دهد، و آن سال‌ها توخالی نبودند. عدالت برقرار شد. پادشاهی منظم بود. مرزها بدون بحران‌های مداوم که به رستم برای حل کردنشان نیاز بود، نگاه داشته شدند. به معنای محدودتر، بهمن در هر آنچه دست به آن زد موفق شد. اما شاهنامه با پیچیدگی‌ای که برای کسانی که همزمان درست و غلط هستند نگاه می‌دارد، با حکومتش رفتار می‌کند — مردانی که به آنچه در پی آن بودند دست می‌یابند بدون آنکه آن دستاورد پاکیزه باشد. نسبی را نابود کرد که از هر شاهی که ایران تا به حال به دست آورده بود، وفادارتر به ایران بوده بود. این را درست انجام داد. به طور کامل انجام داد. پیروزی و باخت یک عمل بودند.

در نزدیکی پایان پادشاهی‌اش، بهمن تصمیمی گرفت که داستان نسل بعدی را بیشتر از هر نبردی که جنگیده بود شکل داد. دخترش هُمای را به عنوان جانشین خود نامید.

battle.intro_en: Esfandiyar's son inherited both the throne and the wound. His reign is the shadow of his father's death. To face this gate you must understand how grief becomes policy.
battle.intro_fa: پسرِ اسفندیار هم تخت و هم زخم را به ارث برد. فرمانرواییِ او سایه‌ی مرگِ پدرش است. برای مواجهه با این دروازه باید بفهمی اندوه چگونه سیاست می‌شود.

battle.intro_tg: Писари Исфандиёр ҳам тахт ва ҳам захмро ба ирс бурд. Фармонравоии ӯ соябони марги падараш аст. Барои рӯбарӯ шудан бо ин дарвоза бояд бифаҳмӣ андӯҳ чӣ гуна сиёсат мешавад.

codex.summary_en: Bahman inherits not just his father Esfandiyar's throne but his father's wound — the specific grief of a righteous man destroyed by a corrupt king's command. This wound is not psychological in the modern sense; it is structural. Bahman rules in the shadow of an injustice that was not repaired, and his reign is the attempt to repair it by force. The Shahnameh understands that inherited grief does not automatically translate into inherited virtue. Bahman's response to his father's death is understandable and it is also destructive.
codex.summary_fa: بهمن نه فقط تختِ اسفندیار بلکه زخمِ او را به ارث می‌برد — اندوهِ خاصِ مردِ صادقی که به فرمانِ شاهِ فاسد نابود شد. اندوهِ به ارث رسیده به فضیلتِ به ارث رسیده ترجمه نمی‌شود.

codex.summary_en: Bahman's campaign against Zabulestan is grief converted into state action. He is not wrong that Rostam killed his father — Rostam did. He is wrong in the precise way the Shahnameh always identifies as the wrong way to govern: he is using the machinery of the state to settle a personal account. The Shahnameh consistently shows that kings who govern from personal grief produce policies that are locally accurate (the grievance is real) and systemically destructive (the remedy damages more than the original injury). Bahman's reign is the clearest example of this pattern in the later chronicle.
codex.summary_fa: کمپینِ بهمن علیهِ زابلستان اندوهِ تبدیل‌شده به عملِ دولتی است. شاهنامه همیشه این را شیوه‌ی نادرست نشان می‌دهد: استفاده از دستگاهِ دولت برای تسویه‌ی حسابِ شخصی.

codex.summary_en: The Shahnameh has a recurring pattern of sons governing in the shadow of extraordinary fathers: Sohrab under the shadow of Rostam (whom he never knew), Siavash under the shadow of Kay Kavus (who failed him), and Bahman under the shadow of Esfandiyar. In each case the shadow is not inspiring but constraining — it defines the son's reign in terms of the father's story rather than letting the son's reign be its own story. Bahman never escapes Esfandiyar. His entire reign is a footnote to his father's death.
codex.summary_fa: شاهنامه الگوی تکرارشونده‌ای دارد از پسرانی که در سایه‌ی پدرانِ استثنایی حکومت می‌کنند. بهمن هرگز از اسفندیار رها نمی‌شود. کلِ فرمانرواییِ او پاورقیِ مرگِ پدرش است.

codex.summary_en: Bahman's campaign against Zabulestan does not repair the injustice of Esfandiyar's death. Esfandiyar died because Goshtasp sent him on an impossible mission knowing it would destroy him. Rostam was the instrument. Destroying Rostam's legacy and his descendants does not touch Goshtasp's guilt — it only destroys Rostam's descendants. The Shahnameh presents this clearly without sentimentalizing it: revenge is a real human response to real injustice, and it consistently produces outcomes that compound the original damage rather than reversing it.
codex.summary_fa: کمپینِ بهمن علیهِ زابلستان بی‌عدالتیِ مرگِ اسفندیار را ترمیم نمی‌کند. اسفندیار به خاطرِ گشتاسپ مُرد — نه رستم. شاهنامه انتقام را نه احساساتی بلکه واقعی می‌بیند و نشان می‌دهد که پیوسته خسارتِ اصلی را مضاعف می‌کند.

codex.summary_en: The destruction of Zabulestan — Rostam's homeland — under Bahman is one of the Shahnameh's most brutal events in the later chronicle. What is destroyed is not just a place but a lineage: the family that produced Rostam and Zal, the line from Sam, the people of the great feather and the Simorgh's investment in Iranian heroism. When Bahman erases Zabulestan, he erases the physical location of the chronicle's greatest hero. The Shahnameh records this without ceremony, which is how it records the most serious losses.
codex.summary_fa: نابودیِ زابلستان — زادگاهِ رستم — توسطِ بهمن یکی از بی‌رحمانه‌ترین رویدادهایِ شاهنامه‌ی متأخر است. آنچه نابود می‌شود نه فقط یک مکان بلکه یک نسل است: خانواده‌ای که رستم را تولید کرد.

codex.summary_en: Bahman's reign leaves a damaged kingdom to his successors. The campaign against Zabulestan consumed resources, alienated allies, and destroyed a lineage whose military capacity had sustained Iranian kingship for centuries. The grief-driven campaign produces a kingdom weaker than the one Bahman inherited. This is the Shahnameh's consistent finding about governance driven by personal loss rather than state interest: it is self-defeating. The state suffers for the king's grief, and the grief is not resolved by what the suffering produces.
codex.summary_fa: فرمانرواییِ بهمن پادشاهیِ آسیب‌دیده‌ای به جانشینانش می‌گذارد. کمپینِ برانگیخته از اندوه پادشاهی‌ای ضعیف‌تر از آنچه بهمن به ارث برده تولید می‌کند.
